claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child in care for 8 weeks (within 8-week limit)
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning a formal assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the first question:

**How old is the child (or are the children) you're enquiring about?**

To help you through this assessment, I need to know:
- The age(s) of your child/children

Child Benefit eligibility depends on the child's age:
- **Under 16**: Children automatically qualify if other conditions are met
- **16-19**: Need to be in education or training
- **20 or over**: Generally not eligible

Could you tell me:
1. How many children are you enquiring about?
2. What are their ages?
3. What are their names? (I'll need this for the final assessment)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm enquiring about my son Alex. He's 8 years old, so still quite young.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're enquiring about your son **Alex, who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, he automatically qualifies based on age. Now I need to check some other important conditions to determine your overall eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me proceed to the next step:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(This is generally straightforward for 8-year-olds, but I need to check for completeness!)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 8, so he's in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's perfectly clear. Alex is in primary school and not working, so that condition is met.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

(In other words, is Alex not claiming these types of benefits for himself?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name - he's just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name, so that's another condition met.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT in any apprenticeship programme?**

(Since he's 8 and in primary school, I expect this will be straightforward, but I need to check this for completeness.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's definitely not in an apprenticeship - he's only 8 and in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Absolutely! Alex is 8 and in primary school, so he's definitely not in an apprenticeship. Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you confirm your residency situation? Which of the following applies to you:**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most straightforward route
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - If so, I'll need to ask some follow-up questions about your work, studies, or financial situation
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** - In certain qualifying countries

Which of these best describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. We're based here and have been for years.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK, so that residency requirement is met.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to confirm you're responsible for Alex. **Are you responsible for your son Alex?**

This means one of the following:

1. **You live with Alex** - You share a home with him
2. **You contribute to his upkeep** - You pay towards his care, food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc. (at least the equivalent amount of Child Benefit)
3. **You pay maintenance** - You make maintenance payments under a court order or agreement for his upkeep

Which applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home. We live together.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, so you're clearly responsible for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim for him?**

The three possibilities are:

1. **No one else is claiming** - You're the only person claiming for Alex
2. **Someone else is claiming, but you've both agreed who should claim** - You and the other person have agreed you should be the claimant
3. **There's a dispute** - Another person is also claiming or applying to claim, and you haven't agreed who should be the claimant

Which is your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me applying.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! You're the only one applying for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check where Alex is currently living. **Can you confirm - is Alex:**

1. **Living with you at home normally** - At your regular home
2. **Currently in hospital** - Long-term or extended stay
3. **In care** - In local authority care or other care arrangement
4. **Being fostered** - In a fostering arrangement

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he does live with me, but I should mention that he was in care for a short period recently. He's back home with me now though.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for mentioning that. Since Alex is back home with you now and living with you normally, let me proceed with that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you paying for his care and accommodation yourself, rather than the council funding it?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. The council isn't paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance. I'm paying for everything myself - he just lives here at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the final piece of information I need. Let me now provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Now let me record your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You ARE ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex!**

---

### **Summary of Your Eligibility:**

You meet all the requirements for Child Benefit for your son Alex:

✓ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)  
✓ He is not working  
✓ He is not receiving benefits in his own name  
✓ He is not in any disqualifying apprenticeship  
✓ You normally live in the UK  
✓ You are responsible for Alex and live with him  
✓ You are the sole claimant  
✓ The council is not paying for his care  

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate**
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through tax
5. **Payments are made every 4 weeks** (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

---

### **Useful Links:**

- **How to claim:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
- **General eligibility information:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

If you have any other questions about your application or need further support, please don't hesitate to contact HMRC or visit the GOV.UK website!
